themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 5 this week versus a 0.2-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1900% increase (z-score: 10.97)—suggesting rapid, unregulated storefront openings or enforcement gaps in Borough Park/Kensington this week.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike, z-score 10.97)
Spike is statistically extreme, indicating sudden cluster rather than gradual trend
No prior local news coverage or Reddit discussion suggests this is breaking now
reporting_angles: How many unlicensed cannabis retailers have opened in the district in the past 1–2 weeks, and why is enforcement lagging?
Interview residents and local business owners about storefront proliferation and community complaints
Investigate whether the city's retail licensing process is keeping pace with demand in this neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Flood Streets
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 5 this week versus 0.8 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 567% spike (z-score: 5.13)—indicating a sudden surge in derelict bikes clogging sidewalks and public space in Borough Park/Kensington this week.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints this week vs. 0.8 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 5.13)
Sharp upward departure from baseline suggests new problem, not seasonal pattern
No prior reporting or community board mention suggests this emerged suddenly
reporting_angles: Are bike-share services (Citi Bike, others) dumping or abandoning inventory in the district?
Interview Sanitation Department about removal timeline and whether staffing is adequate
Check if nearby bike shops or repair facilities have closed, leaving bikes stranded

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signs Spike 600%
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints hit 7 last week versus 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 600% increase (z-score: 8.49)—suggesting systematic removal, theft, or deterioration of directional and informational signage across the district last week.
evidence: 7 missing street sign complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (600% spike, z-score 8.49)
Concentrated spike suggests either coordinated theft, poor maintenance cycle, or weather event
Community board budget repeatedly requests additional DOB building inspectors but no mention of sign maintenance
reporting_angles: Did a construction project or weather event last week damage or remove signs across multiple blocks?
Interview Department of Transportation about inspection frequency and replacement timelines in this district
Check whether sign theft is being prosecuted or if the district is a target for copper/metal scavenging

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Unsanitary Conditions Rise
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 4 last week (700% spike, z-score: 4.95) and unsanitary condition complaints hit 34 last week (98% spike, z-score: 3.69)—both well above baseline—signaling deteriorating street conditions and possible homelessness clustering in Borough Park/Kensington over the last week.
evidence: Encampment complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 4.95)
Unsanitary condition complaints: 34 last week vs. 17.1 weekly average (98% increase, z-score 3.69)
Dual spike suggests interconnected problem—encampments creating unsanitary conditions—rather than isolated issues
reporting_angles: Has a new encampment cluster emerged in a specific area (park, parking lot, underpass) in the past 1–2 weeks?
Interview Department of Homeless Services and NYPD about outreach and enforcement responses
Document conditions on the ground: how many people, what services are lacking, what are residents' safety concerns?

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 9 two weeks ago versus 3.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 188% spike (z-score: 3.47)—suggesting deteriorating sanitation or food storage practices fueling pest activity across Borough Park/Kensington over the past two weeks.
evidence: 9 rodent complaints two weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average (188% spike, z-score 3.47)
Timing aligns with unsanitary condition and encampment spike, suggesting shared root cause (inadequate sanitation oversight)
Heat/hot water complaints remain chronically high (1325 over 90 days), suggesting deteriorating housing conditions that enable pests
reporting_angles: Are specific buildings or blocks more affected, and do they share housing code violations or sanitation failures?
Interview Department of Health and Mental Hygiene about trap placement, poison distribution, and inspection schedules
Investigate whether the district's repeated budget requests for additional building inspectors reflect inadequate housing oversight
